learning_objectives: Identify the three core components of an effective AI prompt: Clarity, Context, and Constraints.
Explain how each of the 3 Cs contributes to generating precise AI outputs.
Apply structured prompt writing techniques, including personas and examples, to enhance AI responses.
Utilize advanced strategies like Chain-of-Thought and iterative prompting for complex tasks.
Format AI outputs using specific structures like tables or lists.
Develop practical skills in both text and image prompting for various AI tools.
outline: The 3 Cs of Prompting: Context and Constraints
Giving Examples: Zero-Shot and One-Shot Prompting

slides.title: Welcome to Advanced Prompting
content: Your single most important skill for using AI effectively.
AI models are powerful, but require specific instructions.
narration: Welcome to this tutorial on Advanced Prompting Techniques.
For non-coders, advanced prompting is a key skill.
It helps you use AI effectively.
Think of an AI model as a smart, fast, and knowledgeable intern.
It performs amazing tasks.
However, it needs specific instructions to do well.
Prompting is the practice of giving these instructions.
This ensures you get high-quality results.

slides.title: The 3 Cs of Prompting: Clarity
content: Weak prompts yield weak answers. Great prompts deliver great answers.
The best prompts consistently include: Clarity, Context, and Constraints.
C1: Clarity means being specific!
AI cannot read your mind; it requires explicit instructions.
Vague prompts result in generic, unhelpful responses.
Specific prompts guide the AI to focus on your exact need.
narration: A weak prompt yields a weak answer.
A strong prompt provides a great answer.
The most effective prompts include three elements.
These are Clarity, Context, and Constraints.
These form the basis for clear AI communication.
We start with the first C: Clarity.
The AI cannot read your mind.
It does not know your true intent.
Vague prompts produce generic, unhelpful answers.
They often miss your actual objective.
For best results, be specific.
Leave no room for misinterpretation.
slides.image_prompt: An infographic showing three interconnected circles labeled 'Clarity', 'Context', and 'Constraints', with 'Great Prompt' at their intersection. A magnifying glass icon highlights 'Clarity'.

slides.title: Clarity in Action: Before and After
content: Weak Prompt: "Write about electric cars."
Good Prompt (Clear): "Write a short blog post explaining the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city."
narration: Let's see clarity in action with an example.
Consider this weak prompt: 'Write about electric cars.'
This is too general.
It gives no direction on length or audience.
It lacks a specific focus.
Now, view the improved version.
The prompt asked for a short blog post.
It needed to explain the top three benefits.
These benefits were for owning an electric car.
The target audience was someone living in a city.
This prompt is much clearer.
It specifies the format and length.
It defines the key focus and target audience.
slides.image_prompt: Screen recording showing an AI tool. First, type 'Write about electric cars.' and show a broad, unfocused response. Then, type 'Write a short blog post explaining the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city.' and show a more structured, relevant output.
slides.video_prompt: Screen recording showing an AI tool. First, type 'Write about electric cars.' and show a broad, unfocused response. Then, type 'Write a short blog post explaining the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city.' and show a more structured, relevant output.

slides.title: The 3 Cs of Prompting: Context and Constraints
content: C2: Context informs the AI about the purpose and target audience.
It helps the AI adopt the correct perspective and tone.
Essential for responses that resonate with specific needs.
C3: Constraints define boundaries for the AI's output.
Specify length, format, style, and other parameters.
Guides the AI to deliver content exactly as you need it.
narration: Next, we discuss Context.
Context tells the AI your purpose.
It also identifies your intended audience.
This background helps the AI respond correctly.
It sets the right perspective, tone, and detail.
Without context, AI content may be incorrect.
It might be technically right, but inappropriate.
This applies to your specific situation.
Finally, we discuss Constraints.
Constraints set rules or boundaries.
They shape the AI's output.
Define parameters like length and format.
Specify a writing style.
List keywords to include or avoid.
Clear constraints guide the AI.
It delivers content meeting your exact needs.
This saves you time in revisions.
slides.image_prompt: An illustration with icons representing various constraints: a clock for length, a document icon for format, a pen for style, and a ruler for boundaries. An illustration showing different audience icons (student, professional, blogger) surrounding an AI chatbot, with an arrow pointing from the audience to the AI, signifying context guidance.

slides.title: Context and Constraints in Action
content: Good Prompt (Clear): "Write a short blog post explaining the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city."
Better Prompt (with Context): "Write a short blog post for a lifestyle blog that focuses on sustainable living. Explain the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city."

Excellent Prompt (with Constraints): "Write a short blog post, under 400 words, for a lifestyle blog that focuses on sustainable living. Explain the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city. Use a friendly and enthusiastic tone and end with a question to encourage comments."
narration: Let's add context to our example.
Our initial good prompt was clear.
It asked for a blog post.
It focused on three benefits of electric cars.
The audience was city dwellers.
Now, observe this better prompt with context:
It requested a blog post for a lifestyle blog.
It should focus on sustainable living.
Explain three benefits of owning an electric car.
The target is someone living in a city.
The AI now understands its specific audience.
This influences its tone and content choices.
Next, we refine our prompt with constraints.
For an excellent prompt, add specific constraints:
It asks for a blog post under 400 words.
Target a sustainable lifestyle blog.
Explain three benefits of owning an electric car.
Focus on city living.
Use a friendly and enthusiastic tone.
End with a question to encourage comments.
Observe how constraints specify word count.
They also define tone and a call to action.
This leaves no doubt about the desired output.
slides.image_prompt: Screen recording. Start with the 'Good Prompt' and its output. Then, add context to create the 'Better Prompt' and show how the AI's response adapts. Finally, introduce the 'Excellent Prompt' with added constraints (word count, tone, closing question) and show the AI's perfectly tailored response.

slides.title: Bonus Tip: Providing a Persona
content: Tell the AI who to act as (e.g., expert, consultant, character).
Influences tone, vocabulary, and perspective of the response.
A powerful trick for specialized or creative outputs.
narration: Here is a bonus tip: provide a persona.
This method is highly effective.
Tell the AI to 'Act as an expert travel agent'.
Or tell it to 'Be a witty storyteller'.
You instruct it to adopt a specific role.
This persona shapes the AI's tone and vocabulary.
It influences the overall perspective.
This makes the output more tailored.
It becomes more authentic to your needs.
slides.image_prompt: An illustration of a single AI robot wearing different 'hats' or accessories representing various personas (e.g., chef hat, magnifying glass, business suit), showing its adaptability.

slides.title: Giving Examples: Zero-Shot and One-Shot Prompting
content: Zero-Shot: You provide no examples.
Most common type of prompting. AI generates content solely based on your instruction.
One-Shot: You provide one example to establish a pattern.
Excellent for specific formatting or style replication.
Helps the AI understand the desired output structure.
narration: Now, let's consider how examples help your prompts.
This concept is called Zero, One, and Few-Shot prompting.
Zero-Shot is the most common approach.
It means you give no examples to the AI.
You simply ask for your desired content.
The AI then generates it based on your instructions.
All examples using the 3 Cs shown so far.
These are all instances of zero-shot prompting.
One-Shot prompting means giving the AI a single example.
The AI uses this example to follow a pattern.
This is useful for specific formats or styles.
The AI learns from your example.
It then applies this pattern to your request.
This ensures the AI understands the desired structure.
It is especially good for structured data.
slides.image_prompt: An AI chatbot receiving a text prompt and generating a response, with a label 'Zero-Shot Prompting' and an icon of 'no examples'. Below, demonstrate One-Shot prompting: Type 'Summarize text into key points like this: Text: 'The sun is a star, and it's the center of our solar system.' Output: 'Primary celestial body: Sun'. Then, add 'Now, use this format for the following text: [insert a short article about a different celestial body here]' and show the AI applying the format.

slides.title: Giving Examples: Few-Shot Prompting
content: Few-Shot: You provide multiple examples to teach a complex pattern.
Ideal for nuanced tasks or demonstrating multiple variations.
Allows the AI to grasp more intricate relationships and styles.
narration: Few-Shot prompting advances this concept.
You provide several examples to the AI.
This teaches it a more complex pattern.
It also helps teach desired behaviors.
This approach suits nuanced tasks.
A single example might not be enough.
By showing more, the AI grasps intricate details.
It understands stylistic preferences.
It also learns decision-making logic.
slides.image_prompt: An illustration showing an AI chatbot being fed multiple distinct examples, with arrows indicating it's learning a complex pattern. Text label: 'Few-Shot Prompting'.

slides.title: Advanced Technique: Chain-of-Thought (CoT)
content: Ask the AI to "Think Step-by-Step" or "Show your reasoning."
Crucial for logic, math, and reasoning problems.
Forces the model to articulate its process, reducing errors.
Prompt Example: "I have 5 boxes of apples. Each box has 12 apples. I eat 3 apples and give away one full box. How many apples are left? Think step-by-step."
narration: Now, let's examine advanced prompting techniques.
The first is Chain-of-Thought, or CoT.
This technique is excellent for logical problems.
It helps with math and complex reasoning.
Add phrases like 'think step-by-step' to your prompt.
You can also use 'show your reasoning'.
This forces the AI to outline its process.
This dramatically reduces errors.
It also greatly improves accuracy.
Let's observe Chain-of-Thought in action.
Consider this prompt:
The prompt states: 'I have five boxes of apples.'
'Each box has twelve apples. I eat three apples.'
'I give away one full box. How many apples are left?'
It instructs: 'Think step-by-step.'
Without 'think step-by-step,' the AI might guess.
It could give a quick, incorrect answer.
With the instruction, the AI breaks down the problem.
It calculates each step methodically.
This leads to a precise solution.
It also clearly shows its reasoning.
slides.image_prompt: Screen recording. First, input the apple problem WITHOUT 'think step-by-step' and show a potentially quick, possibly incorrect answer. Then, input the SAME problem WITH 'think step-by-step' and show the AI meticulously listing each calculation: '1. Total apples: 5 boxes * 12 apples/box = 60 apples. 2. Apples after eating: 60 - 3 = 57 apples. 3. Apples given away: 1 box * 12 apples/box = 12 apples. 4. Apples left: 57 - 12 = 45 apples.'
slides.video_prompt: Screen recording. First, input the apple problem WITHOUT 'think step-by-step' and show a potentially quick, possibly incorrect answer. Then, input the SAME problem WITH 'think step-by-step' and show the AI meticulously listing each calculation: '1. Total apples: 5 boxes * 12 apples/box = 60 apples. 2. Apples after eating: 60 - 3 = 57 apples. 3. Apples given away: 1 box * 12 apples/box = 12 apples. 4. Apples left: 57 - 12 = 45 apples.'

slides.title: Advanced Technique: Structuring the Output
content: Tell the AI the exact format you need.
Saves time organizing information manually.
Examples: numbered lists, HTML, JSON, Markdown tables, CSV.
Prompt Example: "List the pros and cons of remote work. Provide the output as a Markdown table with two columns: 'Pros' and 'Cons'."
narration: Structuring the output is another advanced technique.
Do not just ask for information.
Tell the AI how to organize it.
This saves you much time.
You avoid manually formatting content.
Request formats like a numbered list, or HTML code.
You can also ask for JSON or a Markdown table.
Even a simple comma-separated list works.
Explicit output structure is vital.
It integrates AI content seamlessly into your work.
Let's practice structuring the output.
Consider this prompt:
It asks to 'List pros and cons of remote work.'
It specifies, 'Provide the output as a Markdown table.'
It needs 'two columns: 'Pros' and 'Cons'.'
Without this instruction, the AI might give a paragraph.
It could also provide a simple bulleted list.
By specifying 'Markdown table with two columns', you get a table.
It will be perfectly formatted and ready to use.
This comes directly from the AI.
slides.image_prompt: Screen recording. Input the prompt 'List the pros and cons of remote work. Provide the output as a Markdown table with two columns: 'Pros' and 'Cons'.' Show the AI generating a clean Markdown table with 'Pros' and 'Cons' as headers, populated with relevant points.
slides.video_prompt: Screen recording. Input the prompt 'List the pros and cons of remote work. Provide the output as a Markdown table with two columns: 'Pros' and 'Cons'.' Show the AI generating a clean Markdown table with 'Pros' and 'Cons' as headers, populated with relevant points.

slides.title: Advanced Technique: Iterative Prompting
content: Treat AI interaction as a conversation, not a single command.
Refine your prompts based on the AI's initial output.
Small adjustments lead to significant improvements.
Example Interaction:
You: "Write a slogan for my new coffee shop."
AI: "Brewing Happiness, One Cup at a Time."
You: "That's good, but can you make it shorter and more modern?"
AI: "Urban Brews. Your Daily Grind."
You: "Perfect!"
narration: Our final advanced technique is iterative prompting.
Remember, your first prompt is rarely your last.
The key skill is refining your prompts.
Do this based on the AI's initial output.
Treat your AI interaction like a conversation.
You ask, it responds, then you give feedback.
Provide adjustments to guide it.
Aim for your desired result.
This ongoing process leads to excellent outcomes.
Here is a practical example of iterative prompting.
You might start with:
'Write a slogan for my new coffee shop.'
The AI responds: 'Brewing Happiness, One Cup at a Time.'
You review this and think:
'That's good, but can you make it shorter and more modern?'
The AI then refines its answer to: 'Urban Brews. Your Daily Grind.'
This is a perfect result!
This interaction ensures the final output.
It precisely matches your vision.

Your Daily Grind.' -> 'You: Perfect!'

slides.title: Practical Lab: Text Generation Challenge
content: Open an AI tool: Google Gemini, ChatGPT, or Claude.
Time to practice combining techniques.
Challenge: Combine Persona, the 3 Cs, and Structured Output.

Prompt: "Act as a fitness coach. Create a simple 3-day workout plan for a beginner who wants to exercise at home with no equipment. The goal is a full-body workout. Present it in a table format with columns for 'Day', 'Exercise', and 'Duration'."
narration: Now it's time for a practical lab.
Open an AI tool of your choice.
Options include Google Gemini, ChatGPT, or Claude.
This is your chance to combine all techniques.
We have discussed these strategies.
Remember, experimentation is key.
It helps in mastering prompting skills.
For your first challenge, combine these elements.
Use a Persona, the 3 Cs, and Structured Output.
Use this full prompt: 'Act as a fitness coach.'
'Create a simple three-day workout plan.'
'It is for a beginner at home.'
'No equipment is needed.'
'The goal is a full-body workout.'
'Present it as a table.'
'Use columns for Day, Exercise, and Duration.'
Pause the video and try this now.
Observe how the AI adopts the persona.
It should follow all structural instructions.
slides.image_prompt: Screen recording of an AI tool. Input the full challenge prompt. Show the AI generating a well-formatted table with the specified columns and content that aligns with a fitness coach's persona and beginner home workouts.

slides.title: Practical Lab: Image Prompting Challenge
content: Image tools (Midjourney, DALL-E 3) use similar principles.
Focus on descriptive, visual details.
Think like an artist: colors, lighting, style, composition.
Challenge: "A close-up, photorealistic image of a cat wearing a tiny detective hat and magnifying glass, sitting in a library. The lighting is warm and cinematic."
Experiment with details: add 'vintage', 'noir style', 'oil painting'.
narration: Next, let's discuss image prompting.
Tools like Midjourney or DALL-E 3.
They use the same 3 C principles.
Clarity, Context, and Constraints are key.
But here, the focus is on visual details.
When prompting for images, think like an artist.
Be very descriptive about colors.
Describe lighting, style, and composition.
Detail specific elements you wish to see.
More precise descriptions lead to better images.
The image will be closer to your vision.
For your image challenge, try this prompt.
'A close-up, photorealistic image of a cat.'
'It wears a tiny detective hat.'
'It holds a magnifying glass.'
'The cat sits in a library.'
'Lighting is warm and cinematic.'
Use an image generation tool.
Observe the results carefully.
Then, experiment with more details!
Try adding 'vintage' or 'noir style'.
You could also add 'oil painting'.
See how subtle changes alter the output.
More practice improves your skills.
You will better visualize and describe images.

slides.title: Assignment
content: Choose a complex task you need AI assistance with (e.g., plan an event, draft a report).
Craft an 'Excellent Prompt' incorporating all 3 Cs, a Persona, and a Structured Output.
Apply Chain-of-Thought (if applicable) and use Iterative Prompting to refine the output.
Compare your final output to a simple, vague prompt. Note the difference.
narration: Here is your assignment.
Choose a complex task for AI assistance.
For example, plan an event, or draft a report.
You could also create a travel guide.
First, craft an 'Excellent Prompt'.
Incorporate all three Cs.
Add a specific Persona.
Include a Structured Output format.
Use Chain-of-Thought if it applies.
Then, use Iterative Prompting.
Refine the AI's output until it's perfect.
Finally, compare your refined output.
Compare it to a simple, vague prompt.
Observe the significant difference.
Note the improved quality and usefulness.
